status: DERIVED CONCLUSION - robust to price error because it is driven by MINIMUM PACK SIZES, not unit prices
notes: SELF-SOURCING TWELVE INGREDIENTS IS NOT FEASIBLE ON THIS BUDGET. Ingredients sell in 20-25 kg sacks; you cannot buy 19 kg of collagen and 19 kg of WPI and 5 kg of flavour without opening six or seven sack minimums, and the cash outlay is set by HOW MANY SACKS YOU MUST OPEN, not by how many cans you make. THE TWO MOVES THAT COLLAPSE THAT PROBLEM: (1) BUY A FINISHED BEVERAGE COMPOUND rather than twelve separate ingredients - one purchase from Aromax, Austria Juice, Doehler or the co-packer's own R&D replaces six or seven sack minimums AND transfers the genuine technical risk of stabilising protein at pH 3.2 to someone who has done it before. (2) HAVE THE CO-PACKER SOURCE THE PROTEIN - co-packers buy at tonne pricing, bill it into the run, and you avoid both the sack trap and the small-quantity uplift, and you tie up no capital in inventory you may never use. PUT THIS QUESTION IN THE FIRST EMAIL TO OPRE LABEL AND BUBEE: 'Can you source the protein and supply a complete beverage compound for this specification, and bill both into the run?' Only negotiate direct ingredient supply at the second or third production run.
